Use case: illustration-story. Asset: ONE illustrated six-panel story sheet for a Chinese history game for ages 4–6. Make a square high-resolution canvas, exactly TWO equal columns by THREE equal rows; each cell is a complete 3:2 landscape story painting. Fine cream separators precisely at half width and one-third/two-thirds height, no outer decorative frame. No text, no labels, no arrows, no checkmarks.
Reference image is only for the project's warm detailed children's-book painting style and recurring characters. Keep the yellow-jacket boy with spiky short hair/no glasses, green-jacket boy with straight fringe/round glasses, red-jacket girl with high ponytail/orange flower clip; no extra duplicate children. Story illustrations, not fake photographs. Distinct believable ceramic texture, fabric, wood, soft lighting, clear silhouettes and purposeful hand gestures; avoid stick figures, icon grids or flat pictograms. Each panel must remain legible as a small choice card, focus subjects safely inside its panel.
Panel order, row-major:
1 top left: Qin-era pottery workshop story. A plainly dressed adult Chinese craftsperson works on a large clay soldier, while a completed kneeling armored terracotta soldier and a terracotta horse are plainly visible beside him. Clearly clay, earthy texture, thoughtful craft rather than battle. No modern children in this panel.
2 top right: Today in a museum. The three modern children are walking and talking in front of a glass exhibit with ancient clay soldiers softly behind. This panel clearly focuses on living visitors with colorful clothing, eyes and movement.
3 middle left: The green-jacket boy, round glasses, inspects an enlarged detailed reference photo of a kneeling terracotta soldier on a museum touchscreen; armor plates dominate the screen, he compares with an actual artifact behind glass. Keep screen image as a drawn reference inside a story illustration, no screen text.
4 middle right: The red-jacket girl only looks at a colorful imagined storybook picture of a clay soldier. Open picture book and colored pencils large and recognizable. No actual artifact next to her.
5 bottom left: Yellow boy carefully observes the bend of a clay soldier's leg and the rows of armor in a museum, safely behind a rail, sketching the visible posture in a notebook. Hands and artifact clear, full face.
6 bottom right: Green boy gazes at the clay soldier's face, thinking about an unknown identity; a soft thought bubble contains an empty name badge silhouette with a question mark. Only this single question mark is allowed; no invented written name. Museum setting.
No violence, no children handling artifacts, no fantasy magic, no readable historical inscriptions.

Each panel is a complete scene, clearly separated by very thin straight cream dividers, characters and focal props safely within the central 85% of each cell. No cut-off faces. Reference is for style and recurring children only: yellow coat boy has spiky black hair and no glasses; green coat boy has straight bangs and round glasses; red coat girl has high ponytail and orange flower clip. All children Chinese, no duplicate characters. Each scene readable at small size, few strong focal objects, no decorative clutter. Landscape canvas, exactly 2 columns by 2 rows, four equal 3:2 panels. Panel1 top left: modern Chinese reading room, kindly teal-clothed adult demonstrates a short clapping action and yellow boy then actively claps with her, his hands visible. Panel2 top right: same adult demonstrates clapping, green boy listens attentively with his hands resting apart on the tabletop; he has not tried the action yet. Panel3 bottom left: at home the red girl practices the learned clapping action together with her mother, warm small domestic scene. Panel4 bottom right: yellow boy studies only the decorative outside cover of a closed traditional book held in his hands, without opening it or practicing. Keep this life analogy modern, no claim of a historical Confucius classroom. Subtle expressive differences, not mocking children or portraying wrong answers as stupidity.

Portrait 3:4 canvas made of exactly two equal landscape panels, one above the other. NO PEOPLE in either. Same beautiful Chinese courtyard garden, spring night, same framing of one flowering tree, low flowering plants, wet stone path and eaves, muted ink-blue distance with warm window light. TOP: gentle thin sparse drizzle falling quietly, tiny droplets resting on blossom petals and fresh leaves, still air, restful feeling. BOTTOM: dense heavy slanting rain with large splashes in puddles, leaves shaken and branches blown slightly sideways, still safe, no flood or destruction. Both panels equally rich and attractive. Difference must be rain density and movement, not just darker color.
